items.headline: Anthropic prices shares at $83, valuing the AI firm at $1.5 trillion on the eve of its IPO
items.summary: Anthropic priced its shares at $83 ahead of its IPO, implying a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion and making the offering a major test of investor appetite for frontier-AI companies.

items.headline: Wall Street tumbles to its longest losing streak since 2024 as the Dow drops 1,100 points
items.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply as AI-linked shares continued declining amid concerns that the AI boom may be losing momentum; AP also reported strong demand for Anthropic's IPO.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks agrees to acquire Applied Compute in a $4.5 billion all-stock deal
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute, an AI startup founded by former OpenAI researchers, in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $4.5 billion; the deal was reported alongside the company's earnings update.

items.headline: Nvidia earnings fail to prevent a renewed AI-stock selloff
items.summary: Nvidia shares declined despite reported strong results as investors reassessed the durability of hyperscaler AI capital expenditure and the broader AI investment narrative.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO surge meets fresh warnings about AI valuations and risks
items.summary: Coverage highlighted investor enthusiasm around Anthropic's public-market debut while citing warnings from AI researcher Paul Cristiano about potentially dangerous consequences of increasingly automated AI systems.

items.headline: AMD shares slide as Wall Street's AI rebound loses momentum
items.summary: AMD was among the AI-related stocks under pressure as the broader market weakened after an initial positive reaction to Anthropic's IPO; the report described the IPO as an important gauge of investor appetite for AI.

items.headline: AI's great divergence becomes a growing market theme
items.summary: Axios reported a widening divergence in AI developments and market reactions, including OpenAI's disclosure that its Astra 6.2 model reached the company's stated high threshold for AI self-improvement.
